'''Rima Khachatryan''' (April 3, 1938 – April 10, 2020) was an Armenian educator, chemist, educational innovator,<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 6, 2021 |title=The ECTI published Rima Khachatryan: the daughter of an émigré |work=Tert.am |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2021/10/06/Book/3706354 |access-date=November 7, 2021 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Rima Khachatryan: The Daughter of an Émigré|publisher=Freestyle Print|year=2021|isbn=978-1-7399652-0-4|location=London|pages=76|language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 19, 2023 |title=Lifelong job faded into legend |url=https://www.panorama.am/en/news/2023/09/19/Rima-Khachatryan/2897581 |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=Panorama.am}}</ref> [[:hy:Հայաստանի Հանրապետության վաստակավոր մանկավարժ|Honored Pedagogue of Armenia]]<ref>[https://president.am/en/decrees/item/3745 Decree of the President of Armenia on bestowing on Rima Khachatryan the Honorary Title of "Honored Pedagogue of Armenia"]</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=April 11, 2020 |title=Honoured Pedagogue |work=ankakh.com |url=https://ankakh.com/hy/article/8804 |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=April 11, 2020 |title=Rima Khachatryan: Biography |work=news.am |url=https://news.am/arm/news/571936.html |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref> and author of textbooks for medical colleges.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Melikyan |first=Hamlet |date=November 2007 |title=Foreword instead of review |journal=Nursing |volume=9 |issue=81 |pages=4 |via=Yerevan State Basic Medical College}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=August 31, 2020 |title=Traditionally highly-demanded textbooks now available online |work=Tert.am |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2020/08/31/textbooks/3383643 |access-date=January 24, 2021 |archive-date=September 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200901194323/https://www.tert.am/en/news/2020/08/31/textbooks/3383643 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=11 May 2020|title=Textbooks, that are never outdated|work=News.am|url=https://med.news.am/eng/news/26084/textbooks-that-are-never-outdated.html|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref>

She is known for her efforts to enhance nurse education in Armenia, that led to establishment of a dozen medical colleges in rural areas as well as two scientifically based nursing schools in [[Yerevan]] during 1975-2015.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stamboltsyan |first1=N. |title=Education as a Unique Opportunity for Life |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2018/04/03/Education/3500747 |access-date=23 December 2022 |publisher=Tert.am |date=April 3, 2018 |archive-date=11 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211194108/https://www.tert.am/en/news/2018/04/03/Education/3500747 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1= |date=May 10, 2022 |title=Advanced workshop aimed at sustainable development held in London |work=Aysor.am |url=https://www.aysor.am/en/news/2022/05/10/sustainable-development/1962792 |access-date=5 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Studies in biography |title=Rima Khachatryan: The Daughter of an Émigré |publisher=Freestyle Solutions |year=2022 |isbn=978-1-7399652-1-1 |edition=2nd |location=London |pages=138 |language=en}}</ref>

In the 1990s Rima Khachatryan introduced an innovative methodology aimed at learning outcomes - ''Underperforming Student Success Mode.''<ref>{{Cite book |last=Almanac |title=Sustainable Development: Education, Environment, Energy. |publisher="Time To Print" Printing House |year=2022 |isbn=978-9939-1-1533-7 |edition= |location=Yerevan |pages=25–26 |language=hy}}</ref> Based on four fundamental values - dignity, truthfulness, fairness, and responsibility and freedom - it was about transforming the educational experience itself and made a significant impact on educational reforms in post-soviet Armenia.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |date=May 10, 2022 |title=Continuing education for sustainable development. |work=Tert.am |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2022/05/10/krtutyun/3799625 |access-date=5 June 2022 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Studies in Biography |title=Rima Khachatryan: The Daughter of an Émigré |date=2022 |publisher=Freestyle Solutions |isbn=978-1-7399652-1-1 |edition=Second |location=London |pages=71–72}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=January 16, 2024 |title=Another step towards COP28 goals |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2024/01/16/cop-28/4063314 |access-date=January 23, 2024 |work=Tert.am |archive-date=January 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240123061942/https://www.tert.am/en/news/2024/01/16/cop-28/4063314 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Background and education==
Rima Khachatryan was the youngest of three children born into a close-knit, happy family of émigrés – survivors of the [[Armenian genocide]]. Her parents - Mkhitar Khachatryan and Siranush Martirosyan - had emigrated from [[Eleşkirt|Alashkert]] and [[Van, Turkey|Van]] respectively. They sought refuge and met in an [[orphanage]] of the [[Near East Foundation|Near East Relief]] in [[Gyumri|Alexandropol]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 20, 2021 |title=A True Story about a life journey |work=Aysor.am |url=https://www.aysor.am/en/news/2021/01/20/A-True-Story-About-a-Life-Journey/1793396 |access-date=January 28, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=January 20, 2021 |title=New book about work and life of Rima Khachatryan |work=Aysor.am |url=https://www.aysor.am/ru/news/2021/01/20/%D0%98%D1%81%D1%82%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%B8%D1%8F-%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE-%D0%BF%D1%83%D1%82%D0%B5%D1%88%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%8F/1793396 |access-date=January 28, 2021}}</ref>

In 1960 she graduated from the [[Armenian State Pedagogical University]], and was qualified as a teacher of [[Chemistry]] and [[Biology]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Melikyan |first=Hamlet |date=April 2008 |title=For the sake of Health |journal=Nursing |volume=4 |issue=86 |pages=5 |via=Yerevan State Basic Medical College}}</ref> In 1962-1965 she attended the [[Armenian National Agrarian University]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 11, 2020 |title=Rima Khachatryan passed away |work=Hraparak.am |url=https://hraparak.am/post/2e15cc260a0c7eb7c80bb9feed357229 |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=April 11, 2020 |title=Rima Khachatryan: Life and death |work=Yelaket.am |url=https://yelaket.am/am/article/1025/ |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref> and in 1969 received Diploma in [[Chemistry]] from the School of Pedagogy of the [[National Polytechnic University of Armenia]].<ref>Rima Khachatryan: Education https://ecti.am/en/scholarships#education</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Anthology|title=Rima Khachatryan: Untold Story|publisher=Newmag|year=2020|isbn=978-9939-884-04-2|location=Yerevan|pages=99–100|language=Armenian}}</ref>

==Teaching and promoting nurse education==
From September 1, 1965, until her death in 2020 - for 55 years - Rima Khachatryan taught [[pharmaceutical]], [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic]], [[Analytical chemistry|analytical]], and [[organic chemistry]] at the Yerevan Basic Medical College (in 2002–2013 – Head of the Department of [[Pharmaceutics]]).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Stamboltsyan |first=Nona |date=October 2013 |title=The Educator |journal=For the Sake of Health |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=4 |via=Yerevan State Basic Medical College}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Muradyan |first=Armenak |title=On the Top of 85 Years |publisher=Lacky Print |year=2005 |isbn=99941-954-6-8 |location=Yerevan |pages=63 |language=Armenian}}
</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=April 11, 2020 |title=Life and Death of the Honoured Pedagogue |work=Yerkirmedia.am |url=https://yerkirmedia.am/hy/article/2020/04/11/4997 |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref>
“She believed that the purpose of education should not be reduced to the acquisition of a certain set of skills, but rather the realisation of one's potential and the ability to use those skills in the real life”, Armenian media reported in 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 20, 2021 |title=A Memorial to Rima Khachatryan opened in Yerevan |work=Aysor.am |url=https://www.aysor.am/en/news/2021/04/20/Rima-Khachatryan/1824551 |access-date=May 11, 2021}}</ref>

In 1987, as a finalist of the pan-USSR [[socialist emulation]] in pedagogy, she was awarded with an Honorary Certificate for exceptional achievements by the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, Council of Ministers, All-Union Central Council of Trade Unions and All-Union Leninist Young Communist League.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Anthology|title=Rima Khachatryan: Untold Story|publisher=Newmag|year=2020|isbn=978-9939-884-04-2|location=Yerevan|pages=100–101|language=Armenian}}</ref>

In 2007–2009 she authored and published two [[textbooks]] for the students of medical colleges, namely the two-volume "Inorganic Chemistry" and "Analytical Chemistry".<ref>Textbooks https://ecti.am/en/scholarships#textbook</ref> For about one-and-a-half decades both textbooks have been the core learning resources for a dozen state medical colleges around the country.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 31, 2020 |title=Тaditionally highly-demanded textbooks now available online |work=Tert.am |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2020/08/31/textbooks/3383643 |access-date=January 19, 2021 |archive-date=September 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200901194323/https://www.tert.am/en/news/2020/08/31/textbooks/3383643 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

“Their [the textbooks’] main advantage is the consistency of the [[instructional design]] and the learner-centered approach to presenting the content. Being able to apply the theoretical knowledge through the application and practice activities, the student is given a broader opportunity for self-learning", [[News.am]] stated in 2020 calling them "textbooks that are never outdated".<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 11, 2020 |title=Textbooks that are never outdated |work=News.am |url=https://med.news.am/eng/news/26084/textbooks-that-are-never-outdated.html |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref>

She led the efforts of introducing in medical colleges of Armenia the new educational program for “Pharmaceutics” discipline that attracted substantial attention of the professional pedagogical community.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Biographical research |title=Rima Khachatryan: The Daughter of an Émigré |publisher=Freestyle Solutions |year=2021 |isbn=978-1-7399652-0-4 |edition=1st |location=London |pages=76 |language=en}}</ref>

==Trade union activities==
[[File:Armenia President awards Rima Khachatryan.jpg|thumb|President of Armenia [[Serzh Sargsyan]] awards Rima Khachatryan with Anania Shirakatsi medal, May 27, 2009]]
In 1969-2020, for five decades she led the trade union of the Yerevan Basic Medical College, which media recorded as "a record leadership experience in itself".<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 17, 2020 |title=Memoirs of Rima Khachatryan, Honoured Pedagogue of Armenia, are published by NewMag |work=Aysor.am |url=https://www.aysor.am/en/news/2020/07/17/Rima-Khachatryan/1721713 |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref> She considered "two fundamental elements – schools and [[civil society]] – to be major topics needing attention to encourage nurse education system".<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 28, 2017 |title=A real coach for students |work=Tert.am |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2017/05/28/coach/3500737 |access-date=January 19, 2021 |archive-date=February 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211194111/https://www.tert.am/en/news/2017/05/28/coach/3500737 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last= |date=September 2013 |title=New Principles of Our Trade Union |journal=Nursing |volume=7 |issue= |pages=5 |via=Yerevan State Basic medical College}}</ref>

During the [[First Nagorno-Karabakh War|First Nagorno-Karabakh]] War for the first time in Armenia the trade union she headed decided to direct all membership fees to the mutual aid fund<ref>Trade union activities https://ecti.am/en/scholarships#tradeunion</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=True Life Story|title=Rima Khachatryan: Munich The Terminus|publisher=Newmag|year=2021|isbn=978-9939-884-12-7|location=Yerevan|pages=84|language=Armenian}}</ref> to honour those who served and to raise money for the College's veteran students and their families.

She also significantly contributed to the elaboration of the RA Law on Medical Assistance and Service to the Population<ref>Law of Armenia on Medical Assistance and service to the population http://www.translation-centre.am/pdf/Translat/HH_orenk/Bjshk_Ognut/bjshk_ognut_en.pdf</ref> adopted in 1996, where for the first time ever "issues regarding legal regulation of nursing, assessment of the [[workload]] and fair pay of nurses and [[mid-level practitioners]] were touched upon"<ref>{{Cite book |last=Biographical Research |title=Rima Khachatryan: The Pathway |publisher=Newmag |year=2023 |isbn=978-9939-884-95-0 |location=Yerevan |pages=92 |language=Armenian}}</ref><ref>Nurse Education Development https://ecti.am/en/scholarships#nurse</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=April 11, 2020 |title=Rima Khachatryan: The Educator |work=Bavnews.am |url=https://bavnews.am/մահացել-է-հայաստանի-հանրապետության-վ/ |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref>

==Recognition and legacy==

=== Awards and decorations ===
[[File:Rima Khachatryan receives Honored Pedagogue badge from Armenia President.jpg|thumb|President of Armenia [[Serzh Sargsyan]] awards Rima Khachatryan with the badge of Honored Pedagogue, May 28, 2017]]The Armenian government presented many decorations and awards to Rima Khachatryan. She was named Honoured Pedagogue of Armenia in 2017, was awarded the [[Orders, decorations, and medals of Armenia|"Anania Shirakatsi" Medal]] in 2008,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Stamboltsyan |first=Nona |date=October 2013 |title=The Educator |journal=For the Sake of Health |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=4 |via=Yerevan State Basic Medical College}}</ref> Commemorative Medal of the Prime Minister of Armenia in 2018<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 27, 2023 |title=Lifelong learning boosts our confidence and self-esteem |work=EIH News |url=https://eih.am/eng/news/437/masnagetnery-patmel-en-te-inchu-mardik-petq-e-sharunaken-sovorel-oxj-kyanqi-yntacqum.html |access-date=April 7, 2023}}</ref> and Gold Medal of the [[Ministry of Education and Science (Armenia)|Ministry of Education and Science of Armenia]] (2005).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mkrtchyan |first=Hovanush |date=October 2005 |title=Worthy assessment |journal=Nursing |volume=8 |issue=60 |pages=2 |via=Yerevan State Basic Medical College}}</ref>

During the Soviet period she was awarded the [[Medal "Veteran of Labour"]] in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web |last=EIH Press |date=December 19, 2022 |title=Microsoft's president warns of talent shortage for tackling climate change |url=https://eih.am/eng/news/423/microsofts-president-warns-of-talent-shortage-for-tackling-climate-change.html |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date=December 19, 2022 |website=eih.am/eng/news}}</ref> She also received the Medal of the [[General Confederation of Trade Unions]] (2017).<ref>Rima Khachatryan: Awards https://ecti.am/en/scholarships#awards</ref>

In 2020 the Executive Coaching & Training Institute was named after its founder,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Anthology of articles |title=DzoraHPP: Look from the Past |publisher=Time to Print |year=2024 |isbn=978-9939-1-1912-0 |location=Yerevan |pages=12–14 |language=hy}}</ref> Rima Khachatryan.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Almanac |title=Sustainable Development: Education, Environment, Energy |publisher="Time To Print" Printing House. |year=2022 |isbn=978-9939-1-1533-7 |location=Yerevan |pages=24 |language=hy}}</ref>

===Executive Coaching and Training Institute, ECTI===
The Executive Coaching and Training Institute (ECTI) was established in 2018 by a group of professionals led by Rima Khachatryan<ref>{{Cite book |title=Masters of the Crossroads |publisher=Freestyle Solutions |year=2026 |isbn=978-1-7399652-9-7 |location=London |publication-date=2026 |pages=283-284}}</ref>. Its activities include lifelong learning initiatives focused on capacity building, developing the professional skills of the existing workforce, and providing vocational education<ref>{{Cite book |last= |title=Ակունքներում |date=July 1, 2025 |publisher=Time to Print |year=2025 |isbn=978-9939-1-2016-4 |edition= |location=Yerevan |pages=26-27 |language= |trans-title=The Heart of Origins}}</ref>.

ECTI has collaborated with the UCL Bartlett School of Environment, Energy and Resources on the development of training materials and educational courses. The collaboration has addressed topics including renewable energy systems, the environmental impacts of energy production and use, and related educational programs<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Circular Role of Higher Education: Co-creating Sustainable Communities. |date= |publisher=Springer. |year=2024 |isbn=978-3-031-78602-0 |location=Switzerland |publication-date= |pages=83-85|last=Lotti|first=Lorenzo|language=en}}</ref>.

A merit-based scholarship was established in 2020 in memory of Rima Khachatryan<ref>ECTI Scholarships https://ecti.am/en/scholarships</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=January 21, 2022 |title=An energy market liberalization training held in Yerevan |work=Aysor.am |url=https://www.aysor.am/en/news/2022/01/21/energy-market/1918872 |access-date=January 24, 2022}}</ref> for scholars and research fellows of the Executive Coaching and Training Institute (ECTI). It was set up to enhance lifelong learning and self-development. The fellowships are awarded by the ECTI Board of Trustees. A total of ten scholarships are awarded annually.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 25, 2021 |title=Scholarships for lifelong learning |work=Tert.am |url=https://www.tert.am/en/news/2021/08/25/scholarships/3686396 |access-date=September 6, 2021 |archive-date=August 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210825155348/https://www.tert.am/en/news/2021/08/25/scholarships/3686396 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Commemoration ===
The most natural photo-portrait of Rima Khachatryan was made by Soviet Armenian photographer Armenak Hovhannisyan in his private studio in 1982, which later appeared on the cover of her book “Untold Story” published by the NewMag.<ref>Rima Khachatryan on the NewMag https://newmag.am/post/rima-khachatryans-birthday</ref>

In 2012 the portrait of Rima Khachatryan in a traditional guise of the Armenian mother with an icon of the Virgin and the Child in her hands was painted by Zurab Modebadze<ref>{{Cite book |last=Biographical research |title=Rima Khachatryan: The Daughter of an Émigré |publisher=Freestyle Solutions |year=2021 |isbn=9781739965204 |edition=1st |location=London |pages=119 |language=}}</ref><ref>Interview with an icon painter Zurab Modebadze (Russian) https://mosip.ru/stat_ikon/352-intervyu-s-cerkovym-hudozhnikom-zurabom-modebadze.html</ref> ([[Tempera]]).

In 2020 the sculpture "On a Step Above Heaven" by [[:hy:Դավիթ Մինասյան|David Minasyan (Դավիթ Մինասյան)]] was placed on the Nork Hills in Yerevan, Armenia([[Marble]]), and [[:es:Ricardo Sanz (pintor)|Ricardo Sanz (pintor)]] produced her portrait from photographs of different years ([[Canvas]]).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Biographical research |title=Rima Khachatryan: The Daughter of an Émigré |publisher=Freestyle Solutions |year=2021 |isbn=9781739965204 |edition=1st |location=London |pages=119}}</ref>
